hypotheses.reasoning: Origin: an enrichment-svc-reconciler transaction (id 82971) was holding a row lock on the events table and had been active for about 102 seconds at 07:41:44 (#3059). It was likely started around 07:40, shortly after the ADD INDEX migration on events (#2062, #2231). Writers queued behind that lock. events-db then raised lock wait timeouts on UPDATE events (#3382, #3470). enrichment-svc's UPDATEs were cancelled by statement_timeout (#3488, #3550, #3732). ingest-api waited on enrichment and timed out (#3497, #3567, #3740). The gateway then returned 504s after about 15-28s (#3799, #3912). The enrichment-svc pool and ingest-api pool checkout timeouts (#4071) and the edge-proxy/account-svc 502s are downstream spread, so I did not cite them. The billing-reconciler checksum violations (#3384, #3413) start at the same time but touch a separate table, so I treat them as a separate data-quality issue. The auth-svc 401 invalid_api_key errors (#3826, #3949, #4052) begin later (07:46) and affect login via the identity provider, not POST /v1/events, so they are a separate fault.

Billing-reconciler reports checksum constraint violations in invoice_archive partitions 2019-Q1 through Q4, starting at 07:43:13. These are real data-integrity problems, but they sit on a different table and service from the events write path, so they are probably not the cause of the POST /v1/events latency and 504s.

verdict.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck enrichment-svc-reconciler transaction (events-db txn 82971) and check why it was left open. Verify the events row locks clear and the 504 rate recovers. Then fix the reconciler to commit or time out its transactions and shorten lock hold times. Separately, investigate the billing invoice_archive checksum failures on 2019 partitions and the idp.example invalid API key (likely credential rotation) on auth-svc.
